$comment: Supabase advisor lints accepted on the hosted staging project (infra/security/src/advisors.ts). Each entry names the lint, optionally narrows it with text from its cache_key (one table or function), and says why it is accepted. Leave the list empty rather than accept a lint without a reason; INFO lints never fail and need no entry.

accepted.name: security_definer_view
accepted.reason: api_external is the external-party API (migrations 0750 and 0760): each view runs as its owner by design and returns only rows the caller's engagement grants allow, through private helpers; the base tables stay closed to external callers. pgTAP 0750 and the 9900 security catalog cover it.

accepted.name: security_definer_view
accepted.reason: These app views read private reference catalogs (settings, templates, providers, units) or mask Restricted columns (the *_masked views, ADR 0016 decision 10), so they run as their owner by design; each filters by the reader's memberships or exposes only non-personal reference rows. The 9900 security catalog covers them.

accepted.name: anon_security_definer_function_executable
accepted.reason: api_public holds the anonymous token and lookup calls (share links, advance and signing links, calendar feeds, invitations, public profiles, brands): each checks its own token or handle, refuses a read-only GET and counts failures per address (finding A69-001), so it must run as its owner.

accepted.name: authenticated_security_definer_function_executable
accepted.reason: The same api_public token and lookup calls are open to signed-in callers too, with the same token checks, read-only refusal and per-address limits (finding A69-001).

accepted.name: authenticated_security_definer_function_executable
accepted.reason: app holds the write and workflow API: each SECURITY DEFINER function checks the caller's capability (private.has_capability) or membership before it acts, as the 9900 to 9909 security catalog and each migration's pgTAP suite assert, so it runs as its owner by design.
